topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing by introducing the lecturer, the course context, and the key learning objectives on cancer etiology.

topics.label: The nature of cancer and sources of genetic mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease and outline how endogenous cellular processes, environmental agents, and inherited predispositions generate mutations.

topics.label: Epidemiological evidence and the environmental cancer risk debate
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine common environmental exposures and global epidemiological variations to evaluate the relative contributions of environmental factors versus intrinsic biological chance to cancer risk.

topics.label: Infectious agents and pathogen-driven carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how pathogens drive malignancy, using the multi-step pathogenesis of Burkitt lymphoma to illustrate the interaction between infection, immune suppression, and genetic translocation.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how dietary toxins, UV radiation, and chemical mutagens cause direct and indirect DNA damage through metabolic activation, bulky adduct formation, and oxidative stress.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, contextual susceptibility, and mechanisms of carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how non-mutagenic promoters, chronic inflammation, and developmental stage susceptibility drive tumor outgrowth, concluding with a comprehensive summary of carcinogenic mechanisms.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying carcinogens and assessing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the mutational signature sequencing, epidemiological biobank tracking, animal model testing, and in vitro bacterial assays used to detect and evaluate carcinogens.

topics.label: Risk-benefit considerations and lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing framing by addressing the real-world risk-benefit trade-offs of carcinogen exposures and summarizing the lecture's core takeaways.
